To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the H63D mutation in the HFE gene is associated with hereditary hemachromatosis and with iron overload in HCV and HCV/HCC patients.
HFE gene variants are associated with susceptibility to HH and to acquired iron overload (HCV and HCC).

the HFE*003 and HFE*002 allele are associated with hereditary and acquired iron overload, respectively, and that the H63D polymorphism is in linkage disequilibrium with the IVS2(+3)C allele in healthy controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of iron metabolism and with the association between HFE gene and iron overload in hereditary (HH) and acquired (HCV, hepatocellular carcinoma) diseases.
the identification of HFE gene polymorphisms and their role on the susceptibility to hereditary hemochromatic and in diseases associated to acquired iron overload.
the identification of genetic markers that may contribute to a better understanding of the mechanisms involved in IO, particularly in HCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HFE is a major determinant of HH, but not of IO in HCC and HCV patients.
the C282Y and H63D polymorphisms are associated with hereditary hemocromatosis but not with acquired iron overload.
the H63D mutation is not a risk factor for HCC in HVC patients exhibiting IO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HFE*003 and HFE*002 alleles confer susceptibility to hereditary and acquired IO, respectively.
HFE gene is associated with HH, but not with diseases associated with acquired IR (HCV, and HCC).
H63D polymorphism is not directly associated with susceptibility to acquired or hereditary iron overload, however, H63D G allele is associated with HCC in HVC patients with IO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
H63D G allele is associated to HH and to acquired IO in HCV patients, and the IVS2(+2) C allele is associated to HCC in patients with acquired IO.
the H63D polymorphism is a risk factor for HCC in HFE*001 carriers, but not in H63D carriers.
the IVS2(+3)T>C mutation was not directly associated to HH, but it is a good marker for the C282Y mutation.
